results.term_definition: A binary system is any configuration of two astronomical objects of comparable size that orbit each other under the influence of their own gravity. This could be a binary star, with two stars orbiting each other, or a binary black hole, where both objects are black holes, or a binary system consisting of a black hole and a neutron star. Objects in a binary system orbit around the system's center of mass. When one of the objects is much lighter than the other, as for a star and a planet, or a planet and a moon, it is still appropriate, but less common, to use the term binary system.
